hook: I want to make every failed deploy obvious to fix

builtFor.context: Railway's promise is that you push code and it's live. When that breaks, the next five minutes decide whether a developer trusts the platform. From your public Help Station, the moments that hurt most are the ones where something failed and nobody can say why.

opportunities.title: Failures that explain themselves
opportunities.body: Show what the platform actually saw at each step, starting with healthchecks, so a developer can tell in seconds whether the cause is their code or the platform.

opportunities.title: Evidence for the agent, not instead of it
opportunities.body: Give the Canvas agent the same structured evidence the person sees, so its answers are grounded and checkable.

opportunities.title: Rules shown at the moment they're broken
opportunities.body: 2xx-only healthchecks, PORT binding, pre-deploy commands: bring the docs' rules into the product where they apply.

body: My background is FinTech and RegTech, where the job was making complex, high-stakes systems legible to the people operating them.
At Youverify I designed transaction-monitoring and KYC dashboards that compliance teams used to make decisions from dense data. That's the same skill Railway's deploy and observability views need.

bring.title: Data-dense interfaces
bring.body: Monitoring dashboards where clarity is the product.

bring.title: Design systems
bring.body: A component library that cut developer onboarding time by 45%.

bring.title: Building in code
bring.body: Working prototypes in code, like the one in this pitch, built with AI tools.

systemsGets: Someone who can improve one workflow, like a failed deploy, while keeping the whole dashboard consistent as it grows.

opportunity.title: Healthcheck Timeline
opportunity.problem: A failed healthcheck says it failed, not why. In public threads, developers lost 12 to 18 hours on causes as different as a redirect, a deliberate 503, slow startup and platform-side issues, while their logs said the app was ready.
opportunity.solution: Show every probe attempt and what it got back, lead with a one-line verdict on who owns the fix, and end with one concrete next step. The same evidence is handed to the assistant.

firstWeek.intro: My first week would focus on understanding how developers experience failure on Railway, then shipping a small, useful improvement with the team.

days.body: Meet product, design, engineering and support. Learn current priorities and how success is measured for the deploy experience.
Read recent support threads and Help Station questions. Tag failures by root cause and map where people get stuck.
Agree on one failure moment to improve, based on evidence and what the platform already records.
Prototype in code with real failure examples, then review edge cases with an engineer.
Share what I learned, the prototype, the trade-offs and a proposed next step.

ask: I'd love to bring design craft, product thinking and a builder's habit of shipping working prototypes to Railway's deploy experience.
